chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, who said:
I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying: 'The quince removes the distress of the grieving one, just as the hand removes the sweat from the forehead.'

key_terms.هَمِّ: Distress, anxiety, or burden of the heart

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of eating quince according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the therapeutic properties of the quince (safarjal) in alleviating melancholy, reflecting the Shia tradition of linking physical remedies with spiritual and emotional well-being. The simile of wiping sweat from the forehead emphasizes the immediate and tangible relief the fruit provides to a grieving heart, serving as a practical example of the Prophet's family's holistic approach to health. It underscores the belief that natural elements, blessed by the Imams, can serve as means of divine comfort for the soul.
